target: new: compound of two values (both hold)
reason: Two values of different attributes run together: curved (PATO:0000406, the rule for 'arcuate') and spreading (PATO:0104356); both hold for the part, so it is not a union and not a new term.

target: new: compound of two values (both hold)
reason: Margin irregularly torn (FLOPO:0991115 lacerate) and fringed with hairs (PATO:0001408 ciliated); a compound of two existing values.
Slimy seeds, pulp and bark have the consistency of mucilage: PATO:0001371 mucoid (consistency of mucus). PATO:0001370 viscid is a sticky coating and fits less well.
'Fruit follicular' states the fruit type, so the bearer is a follicle fruit, not a quality. 'Composé de follicules' is an aggregate of follicles.
Semiscandent means half-climbing or leaning on other plants, the way 'scrambling' is used; the earlier review sent 'scrambling' to FLOPO climbing as well.
Lunulate means shaped like a small crescent; this follows rule C314, which sends 'lunate' to PATO:0001870.

label: submarginal
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being located near, but not on, the margin of the structure that bears it. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991208 marginal.
reason: Common for sori, soral lines and veins near the margin. PATO has only peripheral (PATO:0002107) and the relational adjacent to (PATO:0002259); FLOPO marginal means on the margin itself.

target: new: chemical content (part has part some tannin, with increased amount PATO_0000470)
reason: This is a statement about chemical content: the substance is the entity and the amount is the quality. It needs a chemical (ChEBI tannin) inside the part, not a new quality.

target: fungiform (new class of this batch, see 'fungiform')
reason: Mushroom-shaped is the English for fungiform; it should be an exact synonym of the class proposed under 'fungiform', not a separate term.
Partly protruding anthers still protrude, so this maps to the broader PATO:0000623 exserted, the same way rule C321 sent 'prominulous' to prominent.
'Inner bark laminated' means built of layers: PATO:0002068 stratified (a layered configuration). PATO:0002124 laminar means thin and plate-like, which is a different sense.
A lax-flowered inflorescence has its flowers loosely spaced; this follows rule C169, which sends 'lax' to PATO:0001802 loose (RELATED synonym lax). The bearer is the inflorescence.
Faveolate means honeycombed, with close-set angular pits, which is the definition of FLOPO alveolate. It is not foveolate, which goes to PATO foveate.
A defoliated stem or rachis has lost its leaves, which means leaves are absent. The stage and position cues ('in its lower half', 'older') belong in context slots.
Non-decurrent means not running down below the point of insertion: the negation of PATO:0001984 decurrent.
This is phenology or life span ('present only part of the year') and has no clear quality; the examples mix stems, sporophores and the look of the whole plant.
Three-nerved is a count of 3 veins (nerved → vein in flora_counted_parts.tsv). It is not FLOPO:0991202 triplinerved, where the lateral veins arise above the base.
With two bracts (on pedicels usually bracteoles): a count of 2 of bract (bracteate → bract in flora_counted_parts.tsv).

'Directed' means nothing without its direction. With the direction it is already a quality: 'downwardly directed' = FLOPO:0991207 descending; 'directed to the base of X' is a relation to another part.

label: chambered
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's interior being divided by transverse partitions into a series of hollow chambers. NOTE: Chambered (septate) pith, as in Juglans; PATO has hollow (PATO:0002078) but nothing for a partitioned interior.
reason: A standard diagnostic pith character with no PATO or FLOPO term. The seed and taproot uses are rarer and should be checked against this definition.

label: fungiform
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped like a mushroom: a broad, convex cap with an overhanging edge borne on a narrower stalk. NOTE: Broader and with an overhanging edge, unlike FLOPO:0991097 head-shaped (capitellate).
reason: Used for receptacles, stigmas and staminodes; no PATO or FLOPO term. Head-shaped has no stalk and no overhanging cap.
Ternately lobed means divided into three lobes, which is PATO:0002241 trilobed; flora_counted_parts.tsv already treats trilobed as a quality.
The hue (brown) is stated. 'Darker' is a comparison without its second term and is dropped, as 'darker' alone was rejected (C242). It is not dark brown (PATO:0001245).
PATO:0002474 bitter is defined as an 'acrid, sharp, or disagreeable flavor'. For 'acrid smell' only odorous (PATO:0001331) holds, so the rule should apply to taste and sap, not to smell.

label: epiphyllous
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's arising from the surface or midrib of a leaf. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991000 axillary and FLOPO:0991001 leaf-opposed. 'Epiphyllous stamens' (adnate to the perianth) are FLOPO:0991129 adnate towards the perianth, not this class.
reason: Epiphyllous inflorescences (Helwingia, Phyllonoma) are a distinct position with no term; the stamen sense is a relation to another part.
The negation of FLOPO:0991100 reticulate (forming a network), here mostly about venation.
States that prickles are absent: complement of has_part some prickle.

label: cultriform
definition: A 2-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's outline being shaped like the blade of a knife: elongate, with one margin nearly straight and the other convex, narrowing to an oblique point. NOTE: Differs from falcate, where both margins curve the same way.
reason: A standard glossary shape (Acacia phyllodes, leaflets) with no PATO or FLOPO term.
The hue (yellow) is stated; 'darker' compares with another part that is not given and is dropped, as for 'darker brown'. It is not dark yellow (PATO:0001263).

label: drupe-like
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having a fleshy outer layer surrounding a hard, stony inner layer, like a drupe. NOTE: For fruits that are not drupes and for seeds with a fleshy outer coat; real drupes are the bearer drupe fruit PO:0030103.
reason: Unlike the obsoleted 'cherry-like', the property meant here is clear (fleshy outside, stony inside), and it is used for both fruits and seeds. So it cannot just become the bearer drupe fruit.
